title: Space Shuttle Challenger disaster
summary: Space Shuttle Challenger disintegrated 73 seconds after launch on January 28, 1986, when record-low ambient temperatures stiffened the O-ring seals in the right Solid Rocket Booster's aft joint. Hot pressurized gas leaked through the compromised joint, burning through the attachment strut to the external tank. The structural failure led to rotation of the SRB and aerodynamic forces that tore the orbiter apart at Mach 1.92 approximately 46,000 feet above the Atlantic Ocean, killing all seven crew members instantly.
probable_cause: The accident was caused by the failure of the O-ring seals in the aft joint of the right Solid Rocket Booster. Record-low temperatures on launch morning stiffened the O-ring material, reducing its ability to seal the joint. The compromised seals allowed hot pressurized gas to escape, which burned through the aft attachment strut and the external tank. This structural failure caused the SRB to rotate, creating aerodynamic forces that destroyed the orbiter at Mach 1.92.

factors.evidence: The orbiter was torn apart at Mach 1.92 approximately 46,000 feet above the Atlantic Ocean, with both SRBs detaching and continuing uncontrollably.
The O-ring seals in the right SRB's aft joint were not designed to maintain sealing at the record-low temperatures experienced on launch morning.
Similar foam shedding had occurred during previous Space Shuttle launches, but the hazard was not adequately addressed by the certification process.
Record-low temperatures on the morning of the launch stiffened the rubber O-rings, reducing their ability to seal the joints in the SRB.
The design did not include adequate warning or detection systems to alert crews of O-ring failure or excessive joint rotation.

summary: Boeing 727 crashed into a mountain in the Sierra Madre Occidental northwest of Mexico City during climb. The crash was caused by an explosion originating in the wheel well from an overheated wheel that had suffered high drag from faulty brakes during takeoff. Fire from the explosion ignited fuel and hydraulic liquids, which grew rapidly and caused severe structural damage. The aircraft suffered structural failure from the fire and crashed into the mountainside, killing all 159 passengers and 8 crew members. The investigation found faulty brakes caused the wheel to overheat during the takeoff roll, initiating the catastrophic sequence.

title: Pan Am 73
summary: Pan American World Airways Flight 73 was hijacked on the ground at Jinnah International Airport in Karachi, Pakistan, on September 5, 1986. Four armed Palestinian militants of the Abu Nidal Organization, dressed as Pakistani airport security personnel, rushed the aircraft with assault rifles, grenades, and explosives. The hijackers bypassed airport security by driving a van modified to look like an official security vehicle through a security checkpoint. The cockpit crew exited the aircraft through an overhead emergency hatch, immobilizing the aircraft. More than twenty passengers were killed during the hijacking, including nationals from India, the United Kingdom, Italy, Pakistan, and Mexico. All hijackers were arrested and initially sentenced to death, later commuted to life imprisonment.

title: 1986 Mozambican Tupolev Tu-134 crash
summary: A Tupolev Tu-134 with President Samora Machel and 43 others departed Mbala, Zambia at 18:38 for Maputo. The navigator used Doppler navigation to turn the aircraft based on a VOR signal, but inadvertently tuned the VOR receiver to Matsapa Airport in Swaziland instead of Maputo. This placed the aircraft on a navigation path 45° off course. The crew failed to monitor the correct VOR or cross-check their position and continued the descent. The captain did not respond to ground proximity warnings. The aircraft crashed at Mbuzini, South Africa.
probable_cause: Loss of control and impact with terrain due to erroneous navigation caused by crew tuning the VOR receiver to the wrong frequency, inadequate monitoring of navigation systems, and failure to respond to ground proximity warnings.

title: Aeroflot 892
summary: Aeroflot Flight 892 from Minsk to Berlin was diverted to Prague due to adverse weather. Upon return to Berlin, the crew misidentified the closed runway 25R as the landing runway due to a language barrier in understanding a controller's English warning about test lighting. Ground control warnings went unnoticed during cockpit discussion. When the error was realized, the crew changed course and engaged the autopilot but failed to increase thrust, causing an aerodynamic stall. The aircraft crashed into trees approximately 3 km from the runway threshold.
probable_cause: Crew misidentified the landing runway due to inadequate English language proficiency and inability to understand the controller's radio warning. The recovery procedure lacked necessary thrust application, resulting in an aerodynamic stall and controlled flight into terrain.

factors.evidence: Due to the radio operator's lack of English proficiency, the warning that test lights were on runway 25R was misunderstood to mean the aircraft was cleared to land on that runway.
The pilot manually changed course to runway 25R, which was 460 meters to the right of the cleared runway 25L.
The error was noticed on the ground but warnings went unnoticed for some time due to discussion among the crew.
The crew failed to recognize or respond to ground control warnings regarding their incorrect runway alignment.
Upon realizing the error, the crew changed course and engaged autopilot without increasing thrust, which was required for a safe recovery.
The Tu-134 stalled during the attempted recovery due to insufficient thrust.
The aircraft struck trees approximately 3 km from runway 25L's threshold.

events.text: Controller cleared the flight to land on runway 25L but the runway lights for runway 25R were turned on for testing.
Pilot disengaged autopilot and manually changed the course to runway 25R, which was 460 meters to the right of runway 25L.
Ground control warned the aircraft about the error but the warnings went unnoticed for some time due to discussion among the crew.
Once the crew realized their mistake, they rapidly changed course and engaged the autopilot but did not increase the thrust of the aircraft's engines.
The Tu-134 stalled and struck trees some 3 km from runway 25L's threshold.

title: Iraqi Airways 163
summary: Flight 163 was hijacked by four men en route from Baghdad to Amman on December 25, 1986. Two hand grenades were detonated during the hijacking: one in the passenger cabin and another in the cockpit, forcing an emergency descent. The aircraft crashed near Arar, Saudi Arabia, breaking in two and catching fire, killing 63 people. The pro-Iranian group Islamic Jihad Organization claimed responsibility.
probable_cause: Hostile act: hand grenade detonation by hijackers in cockpit and cabin.
